title: Ceasefire or collapse: Ukraine, November 2026
oneLine: Russia's offensive has stalled, the US wants a deal, and the gap is Donetsk: Moscow demands all of it, Kyiv says no land goes without a national vote.

whoIsWho.stance: No withdrawal from Donetsk without a referendum; needs Western money, weapons and guarantees.
The rest of Donetsk first, then a ceasefire; talks continue, so does the war.
Wants a deal fast, with a 'free economic zone' in Donetsk on the table, and no US troops.
Britain, France and others offer a European force, but only after a ceasefire.

whyItMatters: The biggest war in Europe since 1945. Whatever line is drawn in Donetsk decides whether Ukraine keeps its strongest defences, and whether a ceasefire holds or only lets both sides rearm.

timeline.text: Russia annexes Crimea; Russian-backed fighters take parts of Donetsk and Luhansk.
Russia launches its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Russia claims to annex four Ukrainian regions, Donetsk among them.
Trump and Putin meet in Alaska; no deal.
A local ceasefire takes effect around Oleshky, planned to run to 1 November.
Abu Dhabi talks end with a prisoner-swap deal and no deal on land.
